lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPowerSolution.TierTightSpine.gqsp_ScheduleK1_135598
lean.plain: One segment per atomic unit of evolution
lean.annotation: `gqsp_ScheduleK1_135598` assigns Rⱼ = j + 1 one-atomic-unit segments to a run at t = j + 1 a.u., so a run at t = 5 uses five segments at that horizon. The ten horizons sum to 55 segments for one run each, or 2,750 segments when each complete evolution is run 50 times; counting main walks by the reported degree gives a mean of 747,268.5 per run.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPowerSolution.SpecsAux.runScheduleCircuitAdaptive
lean.plain: Segment repetition between initialization and cleanup
lean.annotation: `runScheduleCircuitAdaptive` runs `dInit`, repeats `dSeg j` exactly `R j` times, then runs `dUninit`. The final program supplies a clean-basis schedule that wraps the segments in encoding conversions and in preparation and cleanup of the momentum sum and phase-gradient registers.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPowerProgram
lean.plain: Circuit for evolution to t = j + 1
lean.annotation: The paper uses degree-135,867 generalized QSP for each 1 a.u. segment and reports roughly 141,500 T gates per walk step. The degree counts walk steps, not T gates; the paper reports one-time initialization separately.

statements.markdown: with one walk step per query.
statements.note: The reference estimate charges one qubitized walk step per generalized QSP query. Since each of the ten evolution times has 50 runs, the mean query count is the arithmetic mean of the ten full-time query estimates, not the query estimate evaluated at the mean time.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPowerSolution.ComposableLiveEndpoint.gqsp_HorizonCertTable11
lean.annotation: The block encoding uses $\lambda=135{,}598$ Ha. The preparation certificate compares $\lambda$ times the selection probability of each of six channels with that channel's target weight, summing the absolute errors. With segment duration $t/R_j=1$ a.u., the resulting QSP argument is $\lambda t/R_j=135{,}598$.

statements.markdown: The improvements above lower $\lambda$ to $1.356\times 10^{5}$ Ha.
